\subsection{Heavy Carrier}
\label{unit-heavy-carrier}

\textit{The two weapons system attached uses two different philosophies. The bow battery is an inaccurate weapon system but fires lots and lots of arrows with nasty side effect and are best used versus units which are easy to hit. The heavy crossbow only fires up too three arrows each time and a far more precise weapon with surprisingly large punch. In a hurry the goblin may fire weapons before all of them are loaded.}

\begin{itemize}
\item Cost: 32ip (96 points)
\item Size: Large
\item Models: \hyperref[model-heavy-carrier]{Heavy Carrier}
\item Type: Mechanical, Vehicle, Tracked
\item Armor: 10/8/6/4
\item Shaken: still [-, -, -] / Can't use weapons
\item \textbf{\hyperref[rule-special-transport]{Transport}}: May transport up to 1 Goblin infantry. Deploy order is Deploy(range=1). May deploy directly into assault. If Heavy Carrier enters an assault, you may optionally deploy the infantry to join the assault
\item \textbf{\hyperref[rule-special-forward-position]{Forward Position}}: [1]
\item \textbf{\hyperref[rule-special-fire-order]{Fire Order}}: Fire and load all weapons simultaneously, with identical ammo usage for all weapons

\end{itemize}
\noindent\textbf{Tip}: Slightly more armored compared to the Goblin Armored Carrier, much better armed and more flexible exit, but carries only one goblin infantry unit.

These have dual use, one is to deliver Goblin infantry closer to the enemy, anothes is to lay devastating firepower onto the enemy.

\subsection{Bipedal Mech}
\label{unit-bipedal-mech}

\textit{These are the pride of goblin innovation, the first tank which walks on two legs. Or at least, that is what the goblin claim.}

\begin{itemize}
\item Cost: 24ip (72 points)
\item Size: Large
\item Models: \hyperref[model-bipedal-mech]{Bipedal Mech}
\item Type: Bio Crew, Mechanical, Walking
\item Armor: 8/8/8/6
\item Shaken: still [-, -, -] / Can't use weapons
\item \textbf{\hyperref[rule-special-fire-order]{Fire Order}}: Fire and load all weapons simultaneously. Fire stinkbomb in addition to two light mortars
\item \textbf{\hyperref[rule-special-forward-position]{Forward Position}}: [2]

\end{itemize}
\noindent\textbf{Tip}: Do not underestimate the stinkbombs, which are great versus infantry, tanks and vehicles. Versus biological units the stinkbombs poison the enemy, scare them, cover them in acid, and if you hit you get an area effect hopefully doing the same thing over again. Versus tanks with biological crew, the crew damage can be devastating too, especially versus tanks which are already shaken. It is useless versus drones and robots. Goblin do not know what aiming is, so fire load and repeat as often as possible.

\end{tabular}

\subsection{Mechanical Fire Bird}
\label{unit-mechanical-fire-bird}

\textit{How the goblin manage to make this marvel of a rebuild mechanism is a mystery.}

\begin{itemize}
\item Cost: 24ip (72 points)
\item Size: Medium
\item Models: \hyperref[model-mechanical-fire-bird]{Mechanical Fire Bird}
\item Type: Mechanical, Flying, Drone
\item Armor: 5/4/4/3
\item Shaken: fast\_fly [-, F, F] / Can't use weapons
\item \textbf{\hyperref[rule-special-phoenix]{Phoenix}}: Starts the game with one reassemble token. If temporarily destroyed in 2nd healing phase, you can use one reassemble token to become alive again. Set speed to fast\_fly. If so, half (rounded down) all +1 to future damage token this unit has. If it does not have a reassemble token and is not temporarily destroyed at start of 2nd healing phase, gain one reassemble token. If, it is temporarily destroyed and has no reassemble tokens in 2nd healing phase, this unit is permanently destroyed. While temporarily destroyed, count the model as laying still with movement [-,-,-]
\item \textbf{\hyperref[rule-special-immunity]{Immunity}}: [Fire]

\end{itemize}
\noindent\textbf{Tip}: Try to maneuver to have as many units/models as possible within range 2 and set them on fire with you ring of fire weapon. Sooner or later you will set an enemy on fire, which if the enemy have no means of remove it, is normally devastating. It is fairly well protected, both with fast flying which makes it har to hit, some armor protects from regular muskets and rifles, while simulatiously requires a few shots to disensamble. If you get to use your reassemble token, watch the frustration in your enemy. But do not imagine it is impossible to destroy.

\noindent\textbf{Movement orders}

\begin{tabular}{llll}
fast\_fly & L/R+F & F & F+L/R \\
fast\_fly & F & F & F \\
fast\_fly & F+L/R & F+L/R & F \\
\end{tabular}
\vspace{1ex}


\noindent\textbf{Fire orders}

\begin{tabular}{lll}
fast & - & Load \\
fast & - & Fire \\
\end{tabular}
\vspace{1ex}


\noindent\textbf{Damage Table: Regular}

\begin{tabular}{@{}lp{0.85\textwidth}@{}}
1-3 & +1 to future damage \\
4-5 & +2 to future damage \\
6+ & As 4-5, temporarily destroyed \\
\end{tabular}
\begin{itemize}
\item While temporarily destroyed, all regular damage do inner damage instead
\item + to future damage does not apply to inner damage
\item Note that it does not get the status temporarily destroyed before the apply damage step
\end{itemize}

\textit{Since Goblin infantry are smaller than the other races, you can pack more of them in the same vehicle. Once the goblin exit, they swarm the place with lots and lots of goblin infantry.}

\noindent\textbf{Tip}: Mostly used to deliver lots of goblin infantry fast to the front, however the light mortar can do some serious damage to both infantry and vehicles if you are lucky. Well armored from the front, less so from the sides and rear.

\subsection{Goblin Infantry}
\label{unit-goblin-infantry}

\textit{They are viewed as somewhat primitive by the standards of other races, and they are easily underestimated, until the Goblin infantry swarm you.}

\begin{itemize}
\item Cost: 8mp (8 points)
\item Size: Small
\item Models: \hyperref[model-goblin-infantry]{Goblin Infantry}
\item Type: Bio, Infantry, Walking
\item Shaken: slow [-, -, Flee] / Can't use weapons
\item \textbf{\hyperref[rule-special-to-hit]{To Hit}}: Take Cover[Sneak][-2]
\item \textbf{\hyperref[rule-special-fire-order]{Fire Order}}: You may either fire a regular arrow, a special arrow (arrow with limited ammo) or use one thrown weapon with each fire order.
\item \textbf{\hyperref[rule-special-evasion]{Evasion}}: [4+]

\end{itemize}
\noindent\textbf{Tip}: These are cheap and durable infantry which you may use to swarm the enemy. And especially with some upgrades and support, goblin infantry can be deadly. Consider if you want to combine these units with some motorized transport. In game terms you do want to come close and personal to the enemy, but avoid assaults. Luckily they are hard to hit and can evade incoming bombs.

\noindent\textbf{Movement orders}

\begin{tabular}{llll}
sneak & 360\textdegree{} & 360\textdegree{} & 360\textdegree{} \\
sneak & 360\textdegree{} & F & 360\textdegree{} \\
slow & 360\textdegree{} & F & B \\
\end{tabular}
\vspace{1ex}


\noindent\textbf{Fire orders}

\begin{tabular}{lll}
sneak & Fire & Fire \\
\end{tabular}
\vspace{1ex}


\noindent\textbf{Damage Table: Regular}

\begin{tabular}{@{}lp{0.85\textwidth}@{}}
0-5 & Kill 1 model \\
6-7 & Kill 1 model, Psychic damage[d6] \\
8+ & Unit destroyed \\
\end{tabular}
\begin{itemize}
\item If one model is killed remove half of the +1 future damage tokens and if killed by bleeding/poison, remove that bleeding/poison token
\end{itemize}

\noindent\textbf{Damage Table: Psychic}

\begin{tabular}{@{}lp{0.85\textwidth}@{}}
4+ & shaken \\
\end{tabular}

\begin{itemize}
\item Cost: 4mp 24xp (28 points)
\item Size: Large
\item Models: \hyperref[model-giant-snake-cavalry]{Giant Snake Cavalry}
\item Type: Bio, Cavalry, Walking
\item Shaken: slow [-, -, Flee] / Can't use weapons

\item \textbf{\hyperref[rule-special-hypnotizing-gaze]{Hypnotizing Gaze}}: [range=1]

\end{itemize}
\noindent\textbf{Tip}: Decent endurance, decent in assault with an devastating poison if they hit, and not to expensive. However their low speed, combined with low range limits the usefulness. The large number of tiny snakes are the real power of this unit.

\subsection{Elite Goblin Infantry}
\label{model-elite-goblin-infantry}

\begin{itemize}
\item Cost: 4xp (4 points)
\item Assault: strength 2/1/1/1 (6+), deflection 4/0/0/0 (6+), damage d4-2, AP 2
\item Type: Elite, Bio, Infantry, Walking
\item Upgrades from: \hyperref[model-goblin-infantry]{Goblin Infantry}
\item May carry: \hyperref[equipment-goblin-bow]{Goblin Bow}, \hyperref[equipment-goblin-grenade]{Goblin Grenade}

\item \textit{Grants its Unit:}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{\hyperref[rule-special-resistance]{Resistance}}: Psychic[1]. As long as at least one elite model is alive
\item \textbf{\hyperref[rule-special-pre-assault-retreat]{Pre-Assault Retreat}}: [6+]. Improved by 1 per elite in unit

\end{itemize}

\item \textbf{\hyperref[rule-special-to-hit]{To Hit}}: Thrown Weapons[2]

\item \textit{In assault:}

\phantomsection\label{section-rules}
\section{Rules Reference}


\phantomsection\label{rule-damage-type-acid}%
\noindent\textbf{Acid (damage type)} --- \textit{Rule text pending.}\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{See also:} \hyperref[rule-token-acid]{Acid (token)}, \hyperref[rule-token-minor-acid]{Minor Acid (token)}
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-token-acid}%
\noindent\textbf{Acid (token)} --- Roll a d8 on the following damage table:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Downgrade from acid to minor acid.
\item +1 to future damage
\item As 2, and if unit has armor, it is reduced by 1 (all directions)
\item As 3, and place a poison cloud [4] at hex, and all units in this hex gets a minor acid token.
\item As 4, and in addition all units within range=2 gets a minor acid token
\item As 5, and unit gains a terror token.
\item As 6 and unit is set on fire.
\item Roll three times on this table.,
\end{enumerate}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{Phases:} Agony 0
\item \textit{Removed:} Downgraded as part of effect
\item \textit{See also:} \hyperref[rule-damage-type-acid]{Acid (damage type)}
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-token-aim}%
\noindent\textbf{Aim (token)} --- Get +2 to hit an enemy. Only valid for units in line of sight of the hex where the aim was given. Last for only 1 round.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{Phases:} Gunnery 1, Gunnery 2
\item \textit{Removed:} Either remove all aim tokens when you fire, or remove one each aftermath phase. Also remove all of them if you enter an assault (regardless of whether you win or not)
\item \textit{To hit:} +2
\item \textit{To be hit:} 0
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-special-ammo}%
\noindent\textbf{Ammo (special)} --- Describes how a weapon is loaded and how its ammo is tracked.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{See also:} \hyperref[rule-special-limited-ammo]{Limited Ammo (special)}
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-special-area}%
\noindent\textbf{Area (special)} --- Roll a die per enemy model in the hex. For each die at N+, roll for damage and and add extra damage to the corresponding unit.


\phantomsection\label{rule-special-assault-extra-damage}%
\noindent\textbf{Assault Extra Damage (special)} --- The target gets one \{version\} if hit at least once. Where a ratio is given, it gets one per \{M\} hits instead.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{See also:} \hyperref[rule-special-range-extra-damage]{Range Extra Damage (special)}, Assault Gear Disruption (special)
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-ability-bad-shot}%
\noindent\textbf{Bad Shot (ability)}\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{To hit:} -1
\item \textit{To be hit:} 0
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-special-bonus}%
\noindent\textbf{Bonus (special)} --- \textit{Rule text pending.}\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{See also:} Penalty (special)
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-special-cloud}%
\noindent\textbf{Cloud (special)} --- \textit{Rule text pending.}\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{See also:} \hyperref[rule-hex-fog]{Fog (hex)}, \hyperref[rule-hex-poison-cloud]{Poison Cloud (hex)}
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-token-confused}%
\noindent\textbf{Confused (token)} --- Only effects biological units or units with biological crew. While confused, any movement order is replaced by a random move. Roll a d6, on 1-2, rotate unit left, on 3-4 rotate unit right, on 5-6: -. In addition, while confused you get -1 to hit.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{Phases:} Gunnery 1, Movement 1, Movement 2, Movement 3, Gunnery 2
\item \textit{Removed:} Remove one token each pre-assault step in each movement phase
\item \textit{To hit:} -1
\item \textit{To be hit:} 0
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-special-cunning-assault}%
\noindent\textbf{Cunning Assault (special)} --- For each \{N\} assault successes assigned to one mechanical unit in assault, add +1 to all future damage tokens. If you manage to inflict two or more +1 to future damage this way, the enemy is shaken. Multiple hits from multiple models with same ability stack.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{See also:} Cunning Assault Defense (special)
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-special-cunning-deflection}%
\noindent\textbf{Cunning Deflection (special)} --- \textit{Rule text pending.}\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{See also:} \hyperref[rule-special-cunning-assault]{Cunning Assault (special)}, Cunning Assault Defense (special)
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-special-damage-on-deflect}%
\noindent\textbf{Damage on Deflect (special)} --- \textit{Rule text pending.}

\phantomsection\label{rule-hex-drone-trap}%
\noindent\textbf{Drone Trap (hex)} --- All units from the team which placed the trap are immune to the trapp. All other units are effectd. Area(5+): roll a die per unit, at 5+, the target unit triggers the trap and the unit which triggered the trap gets a minor acid token.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{Removed:} Trap is removed only after triggered
\item \textit{See also:} \hyperref[rule-special-trap]{Trap (special)}, \hyperref[rule-hex-goblin-acid-trap]{Goblin Acid Trap (hex)}
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-ability-enhanced-accuracy}%
\noindent\textbf{Enhanced Accuracy (ability)}\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{To hit:} +1
\item \textit{To be hit:} 0
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-alias-enhanced-arrow}%
\noindent\textbf{Enhanced Arrow} --- see \hyperref[rule-special-to-hit]{To Hit (special)}

\phantomsection\label{rule-special-evasion}%
\noindent\textbf{Evasion (special)} --- Roll a die per area of effect damage. Ignore the damage at \{N\}+


\phantomsection\label{rule-ability-excellent-shot}%
\noindent\textbf{Excellent Shot (ability)}\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{To hit:} +2
\item \textit{To be hit:} 0
\item \textit{See also:} Superb Shot (ability)
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-damage-type-fire}%
\noindent\textbf{Fire (damage type)} --- \textit{Rule text pending.}\begin{itemize}

\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-token-fire}%
\noindent\textbf{Fire (token)} --- Role a d6 and suptracked unit fire resistance if any. If this number is 1 or below, fire is removed. Otherwise\_
\begin{itemize}
\item Ignore armor and regular damage resistance
\item Apply bonus to damage based on the number +future damage tokens
\item Apply damage to the regular damage table  (apply damage after you roll damage for all fire tokens)
\end{itemize}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{Phases:} Agony 2
\item \textit{Removed:} Only as part of effect
\item \textit{See also:} \hyperref[rule-damage-type-fire]{Fire (damage type)}, \hyperref[rule-special-resistance]{Resistance (special)}
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-special-fire-order}%
\noindent\textbf{Fire Order (special)} --- \textit{Rule text pending.}

\phantomsection\label{rule-hex-fog}%
\noindent\textbf{Fog (hex)} --- Treat hex as if it blocks line of sight and gives to-hit penalties for units standing in fog. To Hit penalties stacks with other terrain features.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{Removed:} Remove one Fog in each hex in aftermath phase
\item \textit{To hit:} -1
\item \textit{To be hit:} -1
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-special-forward-position}%
\noindent\textbf{Forward Position (special)} --- At setup this unit may setup upt to \{N\} hexes away from normal setup area.


\phantomsection\label{rule-hex-goblin-acid-trap}%
\noindent\textbf{Goblin Acid Trap (hex)} --- All flying or floating units are immune to the trapp. All other units, including the goblin, are effectd. Roll a die per unit, at 5+, the target unit triggers the trap and the unit which triggered the trap gets an acid token.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{Removed:} Trap is removed only after triggered
\item \textit{See also:} \hyperref[rule-special-trap]{Trap (special)}, \hyperref[rule-hex-drone-trap]{Drone Trap (hex)}
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-ability-good-shot}%
\noindent\textbf{Good Shot (ability)}\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{To hit:} +1
\item \textit{To be hit:} 0
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-special-hidden}%
\noindent\textbf{Hidden (special)} --- \textit{Rule text pending.}\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{See also:} \hyperref[rule-token-hidden]{Hidden (token)}, Hide (special)
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-token-hidden}%
\noindent\textbf{Hidden (token)} --- While hidden you cannot be fired upon or be assaulted, nor can you fire or assault. You are also immune to Fear and Terror,

While hidden replace the unit with a hidden token. If you have multiple hidden units you do not have to reveal which one is under which token (but you have to keep track your self). In the start of the game you do not have to show the enemy exactly what units you have hidden. (but you have to state how many victory points worth of units that are hidden),

Reveal order: Place your unit within 2 hexes of the hidden token and gain reveal bonuses. In addition to revealing your self as a movement order, you may reveal your self any time you share an hex with an enemy. If so, make an assault and gain the stated reveal bonuses

If you reveal your self you get reveal bonuses: +2 to hit of ranged weapons and plus 50 percent assault strength and deflection for the first assault you participate in this round.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{Removed:} You stay hidden until you reveal yourself, in aftermath phase if an enemy is within point blank range, or an enemy special action reveals your location. Cloaking devices stay hidden even if in clear terrain, while all others sources of hidden abilities are revealed if they are in slow or fast in clear terrain within line of sight to an enemy. You only get reveal bonuses if you willingly reveal your self, not if you are forced to.
\item \textit{See also:} Hide (special), Fear (special), \hyperref[rule-special-terror]{Terror (special)}
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-token-hypnotized}%
\noindent\textbf{Hypnotized (token)} --- Can only be given to bio units which are already shaken, and not insane. Any flee order is treatet as do nothing, stand still. In addition, Reduce assault strength 50\% rounded down.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{Phases:} Movement 1, Movement 2, Movement 3
\item \textit{Removed:} When unit is not longer shaken
\item \textit{See also:} \hyperref[rule-token-shaken]{Shaken (token)}, \hyperref[rule-token-insane]{Insane (token)}, \hyperref[rule-special-hypnotizing-gaze]{Hypnotizing Gaze (special)}
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-special-hypnotizing-gaze}%
\noindent\textbf{Hypnotizing Gaze (special)} --- In agony 3, all units that are shaken within range of given unit, also becomes hyptnotized
\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{See also:} \hyperref[rule-token-shaken]{Shaken (token)}
\end{itemize}

\phantomsection\label{rule-token-insane}%
\noindent\textbf{Insane (token)} --- Can only be given to bio units which are already shaken. If also hypnotized, remove hyptnotized token and replace it with insane. Any flee order is treatet at chase, but targets friends or foe alike. If there are two or more equally valid hexes to move to with chase, the owner still decides where to go
\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{Phases:} Movement 1, Movement 2, Movement 3
\item \textit{Removed:} When unit is not longer shaken
\item \textit{See also:} \hyperref[rule-token-shaken]{Shaken (token)}, \hyperref[rule-token-hypnotized]{Hypnotized (token)}, Insanity Field (special)
\end{itemize}

\phantomsection\label{rule-token-poison}%
\noindent\textbf{Poison (token)} --- Roll a d\{N\}.
\begin{itemize}
\item Ignore armor and regular damage resistances
\item Reduce damage by poison resistances of target
\item Apply bonus to damage based on the number +future damage tokens
\item Apply damage to the regular damage table.
\item If poison killed a model, remove poison.
\end{itemize}

If poison did not kill a model, downgrade poison one step
\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{Phases:} Agony 3
\item \textit{See also:} \hyperref[rule-damage-type-poison]{Poison (damage type)}, \hyperref[rule-special-resistance]{Resistance (special)}
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-hex-poison-cloud}%

\begin{itemize}
\item \textit{Removed:} Remove one Poison Cloud in each hex in aftermath phase
\item \textit{See also:} \hyperref[rule-damage-type-poison]{Poison (damage type)}
\end{itemize}


\phantomsection\label{rule-special-pre-assault-retreat}%
\noindent\textbf{Pre-Assault Retreat (special)} --- In pre-assault phase you may roll a die. At N+ you may retreat before the assaults starts. Treat this as a regular reatreat but give or take no assault damage. This ability may only be used if the hex retreating into neither becomes overcrowded, is an illegal hex or contain enemies.
